source: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 17 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 17
knowledgePattern: Convert equality of transformed graphs into a reflection identity
solution:
The two transformed functions are g(x)=f(−2x) and h(x)=f(2x+2). Put u=−2x. Their equality is equivalent to f(u)=f(2−u) for every real u: reflection symmetry about the line x = 1.

B and C express that exact symmetry, so they are necessary as well as sufficient. A checks only two individual inputs and does not ensure a full identity. E uses the wrong symmetry centre.

For D, each term satisfies cos(πk(2−u))=cos(2πk−πku)=cos(πku) for integer k. Thus the sum has the required symmetry and is sufficient. It is not necessary: the zero function has the symmetry but is not the proposed sum, which equals 10 at zero.

F fails the reflection test at u=1/2 and u=3/2, where its values are 1 and -1. Thus D is the required sufficient but not necessary condition. For a counterexample to A, f(u)=u(u−1)(u−2) agrees at 0 and 2 but is not symmetric about 1. For E, (u−1/2)2 has its stated symmetry but the wrong centre. Answer D.

hints.title: Write g and h as formulas
hints.body: A horizontal scale factor of one half replaces x by 2x. A shift one unit left replaces x by x + 1. Apply the operations in the order given.
hints.recap: For a left shift, replace every x in the current formula with x + 1.
hints.pitfall: Use brackets before multiplying a shifted input.
hints.pause: Write g(x) and h(x) in terms of f.

recall.reminder: For a left shift, replace every x in the current formula with x + 1.

hints.title: Compare the two inputs
hints.body: Call the input inside g the new variable u. Rewrite the input inside h using u. On a number line, look for the midpoint of those two inputs.
hints.recap: Equal function values at every pair of reflected inputs describe a line of symmetry.
hints.pitfall: Checking one pair of inputs does not prove an identity for every x.
hints.pause: Write the symmetry condition that f must satisfy.

recall.reminder: Equal function values at every pair of reflected inputs describe a line of symmetry.

hints.title: Test the proposed functions
hints.body: For each explicit formula, replace its input with the reflected input you found. Use cosine’s even symmetry and the period of sine and cosine to simplify.
hints.recap: A necessary condition must hold for every function with the stated symmetry.
hints.pitfall: Sine is odd, so reflecting its input can change its sign.
hints.pause: Find a condition that guarantees the symmetry but is not required for it.

recall.reminder: A necessary condition must hold for every function with the stated symmetry.
